title: AEN descriptor (prototype 0.1, draft)
description: What a business, vendor or directory publishes at /.well-known/aen.json: its identity, search keys and the schema of its actions (how to call it). Never business data (prices, menus, availability, descriptions, addresses, policies): agents get that by calling the business. Public, and never contains secrets.

id.description: The host this descriptor is served from. Directories check it against the URL they fetched it from.

url.description: Base URL that action paths are resolved against. HTTPS is required; plain HTTP is allowed only for loopback addresses, for local development.

signing.description: Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of this document (with signing.signature removed). Pin the key in DNS: _aen.<host> TXT "v=aen1; key=sha256:<hex of the raw public key>".

events.description: Optional Server-Sent Events stream. Emits `descriptor-changed` so a directory can re-fetch at once. It carries no data to trust, only a hint.

keywords.description: Search keys the business lets directories index (with name, categories, capabilities and countries).

countries.description: Search keys: ISO country codes where the business operates.

payment.description: How the business takes payment. handoff: the user pays on the provider's own page. token: the user's own wallet issues a one-time token for exactly the confirmed amount and the agent sends it in order.pay. AEN never carries card data and never moves money; a token is opaque to AEN and its format belongs to the payment provider (tokenTypes names it, for example test.token).

capability.description: A small core set the Foundation defines (catalog.search, availability.check, contact.request, order.create, order.pay, order.status, directory.search), or an extension named x.<namespace>.<name>. Everything else about an action (its input and output) is described by the business, not by AEN.

path.description: Relative to url. {name} segments are filled from the input.

input.description: JSON Schema of the input object.

auth.description: oauth2-device: the user approves on the business's own page (RFC 8628 style); tokens are bound to the agent's key (DPoP style).

description.description: What this action does, in plain words, for an agent that does not know the capability.

output.description: JSON Schema of the response, so an agent knows what it gets back.

sharesPersonalData.description: Which input fields carry the user's personal data, what kind, and why. A client shows this when the user confirms, and sends no field the action does not declare. A field not listed here is not claimed to be non-personal: this is a duty of the business to state, not a detector.

allOf.description: An action with side effects must always ask the user.
A payment action is a side-effecting action.
